notable_absence.finding: The file is only 28 lines long and ends abruptly right after the Table 1 role catalog - it has no 'See Also' section at all, unlike every other page in cloud/projects/ in this batch (projects.md, manage-projects.md, manage-project-users.md all have one, and all three link back to project-roles.md). This is a one-directional link gap: 3 sibling pages point here, but this page points to none of them.

cross_component_finding: This is the central finding for this batch's hypothesis. project-roles.md's own catalog names FIVE roles - Project Owner, Cluster Manager, Cluster Viewer, Data Reader, Data Writer - not the 3-role capella-role:* catalog assembled from SQL++ statement-page citations (organization-owner/project-owner/project-data-writer) in prior rounds. Only 'Project Owner' appears verbatim in both. Critically, the registry's 'project-data-writer' role does NOT appear anywhere on this page - the page's own name for the closest-matching role is just 'Data Writer'. Separately, cloud/security/cmek.json (same batch) cites this exact page's 'Cluster Manager' role as 'Project/Cluster Manager' with anchor '#project-cluster-manager-role', which doesn't match this page's own 'Cluster Manager' label - a second, independent naming-drift instance found by cross-referencing this page against a page that links into it. Net conclusion: the UI/API-facing Project Roles documentation reveals a materially larger and more nuanced role catalog than the statement pages' distant citations ever showed, confirming the batch hypothesis's second branch (more roles/nuance, not the same catalog).
cross_product_finding: None - this page has no server/ RBAC content; Capella's org/project role model is confirmed here (again) as a wholly separate, non-privilege-list access-control shape from server/'s RBAC.
